scene_text: INT. BATHROOM - NIGHT. A cramped bathroom set, 4 by 3.5 metres. A sink and mirror cabinet on the back wall, a bathtub along the right wall with its curtain drawn. NORA (40s) washes her face at the sink, eyes closed. She looks up into the mirror: nothing. She opens the cabinet, closes it — and in the mirror a pale woman now stands behind her, by the bathtub. Nora spins around. Nobody there. Slow Dutch drift during the washing, a mirror reveal, and a fast turn-around reveal of the empty bathtub.

beats.description: Nora leans over the sink, eyes closed, water running. Slow Dutch drift begins.
She straightens and looks into the mirror: only her own reflection.
She opens the cabinet, rummages, closes it.
In the mirror, the Pale Woman now stands behind her by the bathtub.
Nora spins around: the bathroom behind her is empty.
She yanks the shower curtain aside: the bathtub is empty, but a wet handprint glistens on the tile.

references.moment: Tilted Vienna street shots, camera canted off the horizon
references.why: The canted frame is the textbook "world off its axis" move that matches Nora's slow Dutch drift at t=0s — the tilt itself signals something is wrong before anything appears.

references.moment: Jack's slow walk into Room 237's bathroom; the woman in the tub and the mirror
references.technique: Slow forward dolly through doorway, mirror reveal
references.why: The patient push into the bathroom, with the mirror on the wall, is exactly the geometry of Nora's sink-to-mirror-to-bathtub beats (t=4s–t=9s) — the reveal lands in the glass, not in the room.

references.moment: Camera pans off Cecilia and lingers on an empty corner of the room
references.technique: Slow unmotivated pan to empty space, long hold
references.why: Whannell's "pan to nothing and hold" is the precise grammar for t=11s — Nora spins and the bathroom is empty, but the camera keeps staring at the vacancy as if someone is still standing there.

references.moment: Peter's bedroom; the camera slowly reveals Annie clinging to the ceiling
references.technique: Slow, patient camera move revealing a figure already in frame
references.why: The threat is present before the audience registers it, which is how the Pale Woman should appear in the mirror at t=9s and how the wet handprint at t=13s should be found — the frame gives you time to search before you see.

techniques.name: Dutch angle drift
techniques.effect: unease, something is wrong with the world
techniques.move: Slow roll from level to 10-25 degrees while drifting sideways.
techniques.rig_notes: Roll is wrist 3; cheap for the arm.
techniques.examples: The Third Man; The Exorcist III
techniques.matched_beat: Nora leans over the sink, eyes closed, water running. Slow Dutch drift begins. (, )

techniques.name: Mirror reveal
techniques.effect: the jump scare is behind the character, seen in a reflection
techniques.move: Frame the character in a mirror; push gently or rack focus as a figure appears behind them.
techniques.rig_notes: Keep the camera out of the mirror's reflection line: angle 20-30 degrees off the mirror normal.
techniques.matched_beat: She straightens and looks into the mirror: only her own reflection. (, )

techniques.name: Pull-back isolation
techniques.effect: loneliness; the character becomes small and vulnerable
techniques.move: Start on a medium close-up, pull straight back and up slightly to a wide.
techniques.rig_notes: Back along the rail axis; watch reach when the camera rises at the far end.
techniques.matched_beat: She straightens and looks into the mirror: only her own reflection. (, )

techniques.name: Slow lateral reveal
techniques.effect: suspense; the audience scans the frame for what is hidden
techniques.move: Track sideways past a doorway, pillar or furniture so a figure is revealed in the background.
techniques.rig_notes: The ideal rail move: mostly the carriage axis, joints almost static.
techniques.examples: Hereditary attic; The Conjuring clapping game
techniques.matched_beat: She opens the cabinet, rummages, closes it. (, )

techniques.name: Orbit / arc around the victim
techniques.effect: disorientation; the world is closing in
techniques.move: Arc 45-120 degrees around the subject at a constant distance of 1.2-2 m while keeping them centred.
techniques.rig_notes: Combine carriage travel with base rotation; keep the radius above 1 m around the actor.
techniques.matched_beat: Nora spins around: the bathroom behind her is empty. (, )

techniques.name: Backward retreat (leading shot)
techniques.effect: the character is walking into something only the camera can see behind it
techniques.move: Camera moves backward ahead of the walking character, keeping a constant distance.
techniques.rig_notes: Long carriage travel; distance to actor must stay above 1 m.
techniques.examples: The Shining Danny on trike; Us
techniques.matched_beat: She straightens and looks into the mirror: only her own reflection. (, )

shot_list.director_notes: S1–S3 are unchanged: the canted sink drift, the mirror push and the vacancy pan all sat inside the reach envelope and did their job. S4 was the problem — the rail at y=1.0 put the pedestal column and upper arm inside the shower-curtain and bathtub boxes as the carriage ran to x=3.1. I moved the rail back to y=0.75 (still 0.7–0.9 m in front of the camera line, still clear of all actor marks and prop boxes) and shortened the lateral travel so the camera stops at x=2.55, keeping the whole arm on the near side of the curtain plane at y=1.75. The reveal is now a shorter, slower creep past the curtain edge with a small base rotation to hold the tub in frame — the handprint still arrives inside the frame rather than on a cut, but the arm never reaches across the tub or curtain to get there.

shots.name: Canted Sink Drift
shots.intent: Signal that the room is already wrong before anything supernatural appears; the tilt makes the audience lean without knowing why.
shots.reference_title: The Third Man (1949) — canted Vienna street shots

shots.name: Mirror Cabinet Push
shots.intent: Trap the audience in the glass so the Pale Woman's arrival at t=9 is a reflection event, not a room event.
shots.reference_title: The Shining (1980) — Jack enters Room 237's bathroom, woman in the tub and mirror

shots.name: Pan to Nothing
shots.technique: Slow unmotivated pan to empty space, long hold
shots.intent: After Nora spins, the camera refuses to follow her and stares at the vacancy, forcing the audience to search an empty room for a threat.
shots.reference_title: The Invisible Man (2020) — camera pans off Cecilia and lingers on an empty corner

shots.name: Curtain Lateral Reveal
shots.intent: Creep past the shower curtain so the wet handprint is discovered inside the frame, giving the audience time to find it before they understand it.
shots.reference_title: Hereditary (2018) — slow patient reveal of Annie clinging to the ceiling

violations.detail: The upper arm comes within 9.9 cm of Shower Curtain (needs 10.5 cm).
violations.suggestion: Route the camera around 'Shower Curtain' (pass above it or stay on the near side) or move the rail so the arm does not reach across it.

violations.detail: The base column comes within 10.2 cm of Bathtub (needs 10.5 cm).
violations.suggestion: Route the camera around 'Bathtub' (pass above it or stay on the near side) or move the rail so the arm does not reach across it.

shot_list.director_notes: We shoot the bathroom as a single canted world that slowly rights itself just before it breaks: the Dutch drift at t=0 plants wrongness, the mirror push makes the glass the only place the threat can live, and the vacancy pan holds on nothing long enough for the audience to populate it themselves. The final lateral reveal past the shower curtain is the only move that lets the handprint arrive inside the frame rather than on a cut, so the scare is found, not delivered. Every move stays on the rail axis or a small base rotation, keeping the arm inside its reach envelope and clear of the sink, tub and curtain boxes.

notes: The scare is the Pale Woman arriving in the mirror at t=9 — she's a reflection, never in the room. S1 tilts the bathroom wrong before anything happens. S2 locks us in the glass. S3 refuses to follow Nora and stares at nothing. S4 creeps past the curtain so the wet handprint finds them before they understand it. Rhythm: slow, patient, no cuts on the reveal. Safety: the cabinet glass is real — no one stands inside the mirror arc during S2. One rig revision pending; hold until cleared.
